title: Latency-budgeted scatter-gather strategy for reranking endpoint
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: reduce reranker p95 latency and increase tail throughput while preserving end-to-end quality. Problem: the current single-threaded scoring path for large candidate sets causes long p95/p99 tails for user queries that request large candidate pools (>=128). This ticket implements a latency-budgeted scatter-gather execution path that shards candidate sets, runs scoring in parallel with per-shard token caps and speculative short-circuiting, and aggregates results under a client-provided deadline. Key ideas: 1) Client deadline propagation: API accepts a deadline_ms which becomes the orchestrator SLO for the request. 2) Priority-aware scatter: candidate list is partitioned into N shards by a lightweight prefilter (approximate embedding cosine or learned prefilter) and scheduled to worker lanes by shard priority (recently-seen/high-confidence items prioritized). 3) Token admission and per-shard budget: enforce max_tokens_per_shard to limit KV cache pressure and bound worst-case execution per shard. 4) Short-circuit early-accept / early-reject tiers: if top-K candidates are determined with high confidence by a fast lightweight scorer, remaining shards get cancelled. 5) Final gather uses partial-sort and conservative tie-breaking to ensure determinism. Trade-offs: slightly more code complexity in scheduler and more memory for concurrent KV caches; however median latency is unchanged while p95 improved substantially in experiments. This path is gated behind a feature flag and only enabled for requests with candidate_count >= 64 and deadline_ms <= 500. Implementation steps are in comments and linked artifacts below.
comments: 2025-11-05 - Triage: scoped as P1 for next perf cycle. Assigned to Miguel. Initial spike approved. PM (Rao) requested measurable p95 improvement and regression guard rails.

2025-11-07 - Spike notes: implemented prototype scatter+gather in reranker service. Mocked prefilter using L2-quantized embeddings reduced candidate set by ~3x for synthetic dataset with 60% recall at top-10. Measured baseline (single-shard): p50=42ms, p95=312ms, p99=820ms for candidate_count=256. Prototype (4 shards): p50=48ms, p95=172ms, p99=360ms. Memory per worker increased ~12% due to KV cache duplication.

2025-11-10 - Design decision: use per-shard max_tokens=1024 and allow per-request override with admin guard. Use conservative default of shards=min(8, ceil(candidate_count/32)). Chosen prefilter: two-tier approach — CPU prefilter (fast approximate dot) then GPU scorer for final scoring to reduce GPU work.

2025-11-12 - Engineering update: implemented admission controller and per-shard time budget enforcement. Added metrics for shard cancellation, early-accept hits, and token budget breaches. Added feature flag rerank.scatter_gather_v2 with rollout plan.

2025-11-14 - Benchmarks on staging: end-to-end rerank p95 improved from 312ms -> 158ms for candidate_count=256 (deadline_ms=400). Quality delta: MRR top-10 changed -0.35% absolute on the holdout eval set, within acceptable guardrails. Noted a 0.4% increase in cases where top-1 differed; PM approved to continue but requested longer A/B run.

2025-11-16 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/reranker/pull/2345. Requesting review from runtime and infra. Code split: scheduler (go), admission controller (go), lite-prefilter (rust), integration tests (python).

2025-11-18 - Code review feedback: runtime leads requested stronger KV-cache alignment (shared read-only cache for prefix keys) and a fallback path for single-gpu mode to avoid double-counting GPU memory. Also asked to add an opt-out: rerank.scatter_gather_disable_on_dedicated. Added to follow-ups.

2025-11-18 - Next steps: a) Address KV-cache alignment and implement shared read cache shim. b) Run 72h canary on dedicated group with traffic shaping to target candidate_count distribution. c) Add deterministic unit tests for tie-breaking. d) Draft rollout playbook and rollback criteria (p95 regression >5% or quality regression >1.0% absolute).
